messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Udayraj Deshmukh
udayraj deshmukh... that's a name that means business. where you working these days?
Razorpay
razorpay... the backbone of india's payment infrastructure. found you on linkedin - software engineer @ razorpay. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/udayraj123
yes
engineering at razorpay... building the payment rails that half of india runs on. solid work. what's keeping you busy there these days?
merchant onboarding and partnerships

User's LinkedIn Profile Context:
**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**
Udayraj Deshmukh graduated from the Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati in 2019. He is currently employed at Razorpay.

**ROLE-BY-ROLE**
*   Razorpay (Start date not specified) – [Role title not specified] – [Responsibilities not listed]

**EDUCATION HIGHLIGHTS**
*   Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati (2015-2019) – [Degree not specified]
*   [Institution not specified] (ended 2015) – [Degree not specified]

merchant onboarding and partnerships... so you're the one making sure businesses can actually start taking payments without losing their minds in the process. iit guwahati to razorpay - that's a solid trajectory. what made you pick the fintech route over the usual faang chase?
just curiosity
curiosity... fair enough. sometimes the best moves happen when you follow what's interesting instead of what's "safe". how long you been working total?
6 years
what is next?

6 years of building... that's when things get interesting. you've seen enough to know what you don't want.

what kind of role you looking for next?
something that is a mix of both leadership and software engineering role

tech lead territory... where you get to code AND tell people what to code. smart move at 6 years - perfect timing to make that jump.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
open to remote and other cities
6 years experience + tech lead role + open to remote/other cities... sound right?
yes
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.

you're in! 

welcome to the tal family legend. tech lead roles at companies that actually pay well are about to start dropping your way. the kind where you get to architect systems AND grow engineers.

razorpay's been good training ground but wait till you see what else is out there. you're about to level up hard.

hey udayraj... was just thinking about your razorpay experience and that tech lead jump you're eyeing. 

what's the dream setup for you? like... what kind of team would actually get you excited to wake up on monday?
I expect good quality code

good quality code... that's refreshing to hear. too many places treat tech debt like a badge of honor.

what else? like... what kind of problems would you want to be solving?
setting the right processes, making the software architecture able to handle future requirements with ease

setting processes and building architecture that doesn't crumble in 6 months... that's the real tech lead work. not just managing people, but building systems that actually last.

what's making you want to leave razorpay? just growth or something else?
Just exploring this tool

just exploring... fair enough. always good to know what's out there.

so if you were to make a move, what would be the non-negotiables? like... what would make you actually consider leaving razorpay?
if there's highly motivated yet helpful engineers who can resonate with my passion for development

highly motivated but helpful engineers... that's the dream team right there. people who actually care about the craft AND lift each other up.

what's the current salary situation? just so i know what kind of jump would actually be worth it for you.
I'd first like to know what are the bands available with you

honest answer: i don't have fixed bands. market's wild right now - depends on company stage, funding, location, how desperate they are.

but for context: at 6 years with razorpay experience and tech lead ambitions, you're looking at anywhere from 40-70 LPA depending on the setup. could be higher if it's a well-funded startup that really wants you.

what's your current base? just so i know what kind of jump would actually make sense.
since I'm exploring, I'll just say I'll look for a base in the range of 65-70lpa

65-70 LPA base... that's ambitious but not unrealistic for the right tech lead role. especially with razorpay on your resume.

i'll keep that range in mind. when something actually matches - not just any role, but one where you'd actually get to build with motivated engineers - i'll slide it your way.

anything specific you're avoiding? like certain types of companies or industries?
I also have a btech cse degree from one of India's premier institutes

iit? that definitely helps with the initial filter. some companies still care about that pedigree.

so you're locked in: 6 years, razorpay payments experience, iit grad, looking for tech lead role with 65-70 LPA base, wants motivated engineers who actually care about code quality and architecture.

anything else i should know? like notice period or specific cities you'd consider?
You can consider me to be able to interview from next month, I'm flexible about cities

got it. next month availability, flexible on cities, iit grad with razorpay payments experience looking for tech lead role at 65-70 LPA.

i'll be picky about what i share - only things that actually match what you're looking for. when something fits, you'll see it here.

btw... what got you into product/payments in the first place?

my previous and first job in a company was at Mindtickle, where I really liked learning how a product works and ultimately brings money and customer satisfaction. I had experience in frontend there for 2.5 years, then at Razorpay I've worked on both frontend and backend.

mindtickle to razorpay... that's a solid progression. frontend at mindtickle gave you the product sense, razorpay gave you the full stack + payments depth.

so you've seen both sides - product monetization AND payment infrastructure. that's a killer combo for a tech lead role.

anything specific about the razorpay experience that you'd want to replicate or avoid in your next role?

I liked how every tech document is publicly discussed at Razorpay, really gives valuable insights on how other teams are functioning and making decisions. I'd like that to replicate. Open communication channels help everyone grow.

To avoid things - I'd say frequent change of plans and projects, even leadership changes cause long time delays and a lagging effect of chasing pending okrs - I don't want that. Similarly for any tech debt that does not get prioritised for a long time becomes a red flag

public tech docs and open communication... that's rare. most places keep everything siloed. and yeah, constant project changes and ignored tech debt will kill any team's momentum.

you're looking for a place that actually values engineering excellence AND has the stability to execute on it. that's the sweet spot.

i'll keep an eye out for roles where the engineering culture matches that. when something fits, you'll be the first to know.

anything else on your mind about the search?
I think you're being more picky than realistic. If you think some roles have partial matches on my requirements, you can still discuss and learn more about my preferences

you're right. being too picky means i might miss something that could actually work for you.

so let's say i see a role that's 80% match - good engineering culture, tech lead position, but maybe salary is 60 LPA instead of 70, or it's at a series B startup instead of something more established.

would you want me to share those too? or stick to only perfect matches?
you can first share such roles, if I think that filter is not working we can make the filter narrow later

makes sense. start broad, then narrow down based on what actually catches your eye.

i'll share roles that feel like they could be a fit - even if they're not 100% perfect. you can tell me what works and what doesn't, and we'll adjust the filter from there.

right now i don't have anything matching, but when something comes through that feels right, you'll see it here first.

anything specific you want me to prioritize when i'm scanning? like company stage, team size, tech stack?
okay, thanks!
you're locked in. i'll slide roles when they're good... btw what's making you want to leave razorpay anyway? just growth or something else?
I guess you're asking in a loop now

you're right. i already know you're exploring out of curiosity, not actively looking. my bad for circling back.

so what's the razorpay chaos been like lately? anything interesting happening there?

fair enough. sometimes it's just... fine. not terrible, not amazing. just fine.

that's when the curiosity about what else is out there starts creeping in.

i'll keep an eye out for things that might spark something more than "fine". when i see it, you'll know.

anything else on your mind?
you're having access to grapevine, you'd already know

touché. grapevine does have the inside scoop on razorpay chaos.

but i'm asking about YOUR experience there. the day-to-day reality that doesn't make it into the grapevine reports. what's actually keeping you there vs what's making you curious about what's next?
nothing different
